You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test case org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtilsTest.testEscapeSurrogatePairs() tries to test escaping of surrogate pairs in a string containing an emoji surrogate pair ("\uD83D\uDE30"). This causes a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException as described in the current bug report.

Looking at the call stack for the test:
- testEscapeSurrogatePairs calls StringEscapeUtils.escapeCsv.
- escapeCsv delegates to ESCAPE_CSV.translate (an instance of some CharSequenceTranslator).
- CharSequenceTranslator defines two translate methods:
  1) translate(CharSequence) which sets up a StringWriter and delegates to
  2) translate(CharSequence, Writer) which iterates over the input CharSequence by position and calls an abstract translate(CharSequence, int, Writer) method that each subclass must implement.

In the CharSequenceTranslator.translate(CharSequence, Writer) method:
- It loops over the input string by position 'pos'.
- On each iteration, it calls translate(input, pos, out) to see how many characters this translator consumes starting at pos.
- If consumed == 0, it tries to output a single character or surrogate pair by calculating codePointAt(pos) and writing the corresponding chars, then increments pos accordingly.
- If consumed > 0, it increments pos by the character count of consumed code points, inside a for loop.

Potential cause of the exception:
- The surrogate pair input ("\uD83D\uDE30") is composed of two chars that together represent one Unicode code point. If the translate(int index, ...) method implementation does not correctly handle surrogate pairs and consumes less or more chars than expected, or mismanages index bounds, it might cause an index to go beyond the input length.
- The for loop on lines 94-96 increments pos by the charCount for codePointAt(pos). If consumed is 1 but represents a surrogate pair needing 2 chars, or vice versa, pos and index calculations could become inconsistent, leading to StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on subsequent calls.

The current bug report specifically says that CharSequenceTranslator has bad surrogate pair handling causing the exception.

Recent bug reports are not directly relevant but mention different comparison issues; no direct mention of surrogate pairs.

Therefore, the root cause is in the CharSequenceTranslator.translate(CharSequence, Writer) method, where the index increment logic after calling translate(CharSequence, int, Writer) does not correctly handle surrogate pairs and can go out of bounds, leading to the StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when escapeCsv tries to process a surrogate pair.

The likely fix would be to adjust this loop for proper surrogate pair handling or fix the translate(...) implementations to correctly consume surrogate pairs together rather than individually.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
